Claude Agent SDK v0.2.165 documents what the winner lacks: typed in-process tools (@tool plus create_sdk_mcp_server, README.md:102-140), Python hook callbacks (README.md:199-246), a can_use_tool permission callback (types.py:2158), resume and fork_session (types.py:2040, 2249), and session_store. session_store mirrors transcripts to an external store, so resume can materialize when the local file is absent (types.py:2403-2410). That gives cross-host transcript resume between the WSL workstation and the Macs; it is not durable multi-host state or replay. Two things changed since the 2026-09-29 refutation: the named --lookup-tool application now exists, and the missing typed tool argument is verified at rust-v0.162.0. One measured weakness needs a retest. The stack's own interrupt receipt shows ResultMessage usage all zeros (terminal_reason aborted_streaming), and none of the 14 GitHub releases v0.2.151-v0.2.165 mentions interrupt usage. The two arms are billed differently: the Claude arm runs on API credits (seed note: 0.2.164 ran the 10-08 API-credit checks; the profile pins 0.2.163), while the Codex arm uses the native ChatGPT account. proposed.demonstrated_gap: The strongest newly verified capability lead concerns cancellation: v2.11.0 adds abort_signal support to Runner, Workflow and nodes, and cancels /run_sse execution when its client disconnects. This is relevant to the layer's unresolved cancellation evidence. It does not establish complete cancellation receipts, cessation of provider consumption, or superiority over current Codex. A concrete requirement for this disconnect behavior must be qualified before promoting a trial. SQLite memory is also newly available, but it is not evidence of durable workflow checkpoints or multi-host replay.
proposed.comparison_that_would_overturn: Once disconnect-triggered cancellation is required, compare ADK v2.11.0 with the installed Codex control and a separately pinned current Codex upgrade. Use the same historical-data extraction fixture and deterministic tools. Cancel during model streaming and during a delayed read-only tool, then disconnect the client. Require correct accepted artifacts for completed cases, terminal receipts for cancelled cases, zero tool executions after acknowledged cancellation, and explicit treatment of unavailable provider usage. Run repeated cases on WSL2 and macOS arm64 using an already authorized provider. Promote only if ADK satisfies a needed behavior the supported Codex surface cannot satisfy, or a matched comparison demonstrates an advantage.
evidence: The October release explicitly introduces graceful cancellation, cancellation on SSE disconnect, workflow tool confirmation and SQLite memory. [v2.11.0 release](https://github.com/google/adk-python/releases/tag/v2.11.0).

The upstream README describes a graph workflow runtime, custom functions and MCP tools, model-agnostic operation, Python 3.11+, and supported installation through google-adk. proposed.demonstrated_gap: No review arm in this layer has a measured quality result, and the conditional review bridge is stale. Open Code Review (OCR) publishes a measured claim against Claude Code on a public annotated dataset: 'Compared to general-purpose agents (Claude Code), Open Code Review achieves significantly higher Precision and F1 with the same underlying model, while consuming only ~1/9 of the tokens', with lower recall by its own statement. The dataset is AACR-Bench: 50 repositories, 200 PRs, 1,505 annotated issues, published on Hugging Face as 2.15k labelled rows. Under the task rule, that makes OCR plausibly better than the layer's unmeasured review path. It also has a native-account route. Its delegate skill makes OCR LLM-free ('instructs the host agent to perform the code review'), with OCR supplying deterministic file filtering and rule resolution. It installs as a Claude Code plugin (/plugin marketplace add alibaba/open-code-review) or a Codex plugin, so no new credential is needed. The benchmarked full mode can also run on native accounts. Custom providers take a url and a protocol (anthropic, openai, openai-responses), local endpoints included (the docs show http://127.0.0.1:11434/v1), so full mode can point at the stack's local gateway, such as OmniRoute if it serves one of those protocols, without a new key. Caveats: the benchmark is vendor-run, measures full mode only, and leaves delegate mode unbenchmarked. Maintenance: newest default-branch commit 2026-10-08 and v1.12.13 released the same day. Its one advisory, GHSA-wwg6-qfxw-xffj (medium), was fixed in 1.11.1.
proposed.comparison_that_would_overturn: Run a same-judge review comparison on the withmartian/code-review-benchmark offline set (50 PRs, 173 golden comments, judge prompts and pipeline, MIT) plus a fixed 20-PR AACR-Bench sample. There are four arms, each with its mode stated: (a) OCR full mode, the mode its benchmark measured, through a custom provider pointed at the local gateway with the same model as arm c; (b) OCR's delegate skill driving Claude Code, which is LLM-free on the OCR side; (c) plain Claude Code review; (d) `codex review`. All arms use the same model per family and one recorded judge model. OCR becomes the review front-end only if arm a or arm b beats the best native arm (c or d) on F1 with recall no lower and fewer tokens per PR. proposed.demonstrated_gap: The layer has no merge tool: difftastic only produces diffs. A read-only replay found 34 merges in this repository's history that git's default merge cannot complete. The replay used git 2.53.0 `merge-tree --write-tree` on all 100 two-parent merges on origin/main since 2026-09-01, which all fall between 2026-09-19 and 2026-09-22; 34 conflict under git's default ort merge. Thirty-three of the 34 contain a hunk where both sides changed the same entry's bytes and sha256 in the generated manifests/evidence.json. Those are true conflicts on derived data: no 3-way driver should resolve them, and the file should be regenerated instead. The population a merge driver can address is 65 conflicts across 24 merges in files other than the two generated ones: 43 JSON, 15 Markdown, 6 Python and 1 other. Mergiraf v0.20.0 supports the 49 JSON and Python conflicts but not Markdown. It can run after a conflict (`mergiraf solve`) or be enabled per repository through the untracked .git/info/attributes, so a trial changes no tracked config. `mergiraf review` gives an audit trail for every merge it solves. It is the current version of the comparator that weave's self-published table measures only at v0.16.3. There is no GitHub repository, so the canonical form here is the Codeberg URL.
proposed.comparison_that_would_overturn: Run an offline replay in a scratch clone, on linux-wsl2-x86_64 and macos-arm64. Re-run all 100 recorded merges: the 34 that conflicted, plus the 66 clean ones as regression controls. Arm A is git ort. Arm B is mergiraf v0.20.0, registered only in the clone's local git config and .git/info/attributes; Git 2.44 or newer is recommended. Arm C is weave v0.5.4. Every arm regenerates the two generated files (manifests/evidence.json and docs/ecosystem/index.html) with the repository's own generators. Measure per file: clean resolutions; equality with the recorded merge tree, using canonical JSON equality for .json; wrong clean merges (clean but different from the recorded tree and failing scripts/validate.py or the tests); regressions on the 66 clean merges; and runtime. Adopt mergiraf, scoped to the extensions where it wins, only if it resolves more of the 49 JSON and Python conflicts than ort with zero wrong clean merges and zero regressions. Refute it if it resolves nothing beyond ort or produces any wrong clean merge.

proposed.demonstrated_gap: GitButler has capabilities that worktrunk and plain git lack: an operation log with `but undo` and `but redo`; rebases that always succeed, marking commits as conflicted for later `but resolve`; several parallel and stacked branches in one working directory; and `but agent setup`, which installs a GitButler skill for Codex and Claude Code. As a replacement for worktrunk it does not fit this stack's lane model, for four documented reasons. First, GitButler's own docs advise worktrees 'when agents need incompatible checkout states, separate runtime state, or competing attempts', and every lane here runs validate.py and tests; the docs say parallel branches 'are not runtime isolation'. Second, workspace mode rejects a plain `git commit` on gitbutler/workspace, and every lane and script commits with git. Third, `but pr new` requires a GitButler forge account (`but config forge auth`), a new credential next to gh. Fourth, it defers conflicts rather than reducing them, while the measured conflicts sit in shared JSON manifests. No gap is demonstrated for the current requirement. It is a credible complement for independent small tasks in one checkout.
proposed.comparison_that_would_overturn:
Use a disposable clone of this repository with two concurrent agent sessions, Claude Code and Codex, on independent tasks, plus one forced overlap in manifests/stack.json. Arm A uses worktrunk v0.80.0 with two worktrees and opens PRs with gh. Arm B uses `but` at release/0.22.3, or a pinned master commit, in one directory after `but setup` and `but agent setup`. It opens PRs with `but push` plus `gh pr create`, without GitButler forge auth. Measure on both hosts:
- correct branch attribution of every hunk
- conflicts surfaced, and the time to resolve them
- recovery from an injected bad rebase or amend (`but undo`/oplog against git reflog)
- interference between concurrent validate.py and test runs
- whether gh PR creation works
- the metrics setting
Move GitButler to targeted only if it matches correctness with zero cross-agent contamination and fewer manual steps, without a new credential.

proposed.demonstrated_gap: jj covers the same conflict and undo gap that GitButler targets, on a Git backend under Apache-2.0. Conflicts are first-class objects recorded in commits, so rebasing parallel agent changes never stops on a conflict. An operation log with undo lets one bad agent operation be reverted. Workspaces are the analogue of worktrees, and colocated repositories keep GitHub and gh workflows. jj ships a default mergiraf merge-tool configuration (`jj resolve --tool mergiraf`), so it composes with the targeted merge driver. Its newest release, v0.46.0 on 2026-10-07, came after the 09-29 metadata screen. Adopting it would change the VCS commands of every lane and script. Its interaction with this repository's 250 existing git worktrees, and gh behavior inside jj workspaces, are unverified. It is an alternative to compare, not a trial now.
proposed.comparison_that_would_overturn:
Run the same two-agent scenario as GitButler using jj v0.46.0 workspaces in a colocated clone. Then rebase the 34 conflicted merge pairs from the replay as jj changes and resolve them with `jj resolve --tool mergiraf`. Measure:
- conflicts recorded versus blocking
- recovery of an injected bad operation with `jj undo` or `jj op restore`
- equality of the resolved trees with the plain-mergiraf replay
- PR creation through gh from a workspace
- any breakage of existing git worktrees or lane scripts
Move jj to targeted only if it is equal or better on every measure and leaves gh-based PR automation unchanged.

FOLLOW-UP ROUND. The critic found that the parallel-agent branch class had been screened only by metadata, and that mergiraf was unassessed because it is hosted on Codeberg.

(1) Canonical form: mergiraf has no GitHub repository (api.github.com/repos/mergiraf/mergiraf returns 404). It is proposed as https://codeberg.org/mergiraf/mergiraf, with facts from the Codeberg API. Search results showed only an unofficial GitHub mirror, which was not used.

(2) CORRECTION: the 09-26 fit refutation of weave said 'No demand' because 1 of 400 commit subjects mentions a conflict or rebase.
- A read-only git 2.53 merge-tree replay contradicts this. Of the 100 two-parent merges on origin/main, all dated 2026-09-19..22, 34 conflict under git's default merge.
- There have been 0 merge commits since 2026-09-23 (625 commits landed without one). October rebases still conflict in manifests/evidence.json, as the receipts cited in the mergiraf entry show.
- 33 of the 34 include a same-entry bytes/sha256 conflict in the generated manifests/evidence.json.
- The biggest lever is therefore regenerating generated files on conflict with the repository's own generators (scripts/evidence_manifest.py, scripts/build_ecosystem.py). No merge driver replaces that. It is a practice gap, not an upstream candidate.
- 24 merges also conflict in 65 instances outside the two generated files. Some of those files may also be generated; this was not checked.

(3) Replay side effect: GIT_OBJECT_DIRECTORY pointed at the scratch dir, with the repository's object store as an alternate. No new objects were created: every needed object already existed (for example, tree b52cf287 was born 2026-10-06 11:53 in an earlier replay). Git did freshen mtimes of pre-existing loose objects in .git/objects. No refs, index or worktree changed.

(4) Winner and alternative health:
- worktrunk: v0.80.0 (2026-09-27) is still the latest. Not archived, NOASSERTION, 9,053 stars, pushed 2026-10-09. The sealed winners entry pins 0.79.0; components_vs_upstream pins 0.80.0.

(5) Incumbency: all three winners carry evidence_class source_review, with platform_status not_established on linux-wsl2 and untested on macOS. Worktrunk's standing over GitButler, jj and coderabbitai/git-worktree-runner rests on incumbency; no matched comparison exists.

claude_discover.notes:
METHOD. The maintenance window is default-branch commits since 2026-07-11 (90 days before 2026-10-09). Every repository I labelled or excluded was checked with REST commits?since; GraphQL counts are context only. Repository permalinks are at 491aceef, which is on origin/main. Budget used: 6 web searches; 3 page fetches (docs.zizmor.sh/audits, the GitHub 2026 Actions security roadmap post, community discussion #194494); 31 gh api calls.

NEW FACTS FOR THIS LAYER.
(1) zizmor has no AI-agent audit. A full-text scan of docs/audits.md at main finds 41 audits and no claude, codex, gemini, agent, llm, ai-inference or prompt. Meanwhile harness-audit.yml runs claude-code-action with id-token: write and issues: write. tests/test_workflow_policy.py has 0 matches for prompt, allowedTools, allowed_tools, claude_args or claude-code-action.
(2) The SHA-pinned ossf/scorecard-action@2d1146689b8c runs docker://ghcr.io/ossf/scorecard-action:v2.4.4 by tag (action.yaml lines 60-61). That job holds security-events: write, and no repository record mentions the tag. The cheapest fix needs no new tool: digest-pin the image, or use a checksum- and Sigstore-verified Scorecard binary, as supply-chain.yml does for syft and grype.
(3) native-offhost-app-state.yml:51 installs uv==0.9.17 by version without --require-hashes. This sits inside a recorded hash-frozen exemption job. zizmor's adhoc-packages audit covers npm, yarn, pnpm, gem and bundle only, so the winner does not flag pip installs.

AGENTIC-ACTIONS-AUDITOR on the 23 workflows. There are 0 local composite and 0 reusable-workflow uses:, and 1 AI action instance (Claude Code Action in harness-audit.yml). Its triggers are schedule and workflow_dispatch with no inputs, main-only. The prompt is static apart from runner.temp, and the third-party audit prompt is pinned by commit and sha256. There is no env intermediary, CLI data fetch, PR-target checkout, eval of output, dangerous sandbox or wildcard allowlist, so there are 0 injection findings. Vector F (an allowed Bash prefix with a public issue sink) is Info only: no injection vector co-occurs, and it was not verified against Claude Code's Bash permission matcher.

WINNER HEALTH. No archive, rename, relicense or major release.
- zizmor: pin 1.30.1 equals the latest release (2026-09-09); 155 default-branch commits since 2026-07-11.
- syft: the stack pin 1.54.0 (supply-chain.yml:81) is one patch behind v1.54.1 (2026-10-06; dependency bumps including go-securesystemslib 0.11.1). The sealed verdict still names 1.52.0.
- actions/attest: the latest release v4.2.2 (2026-08-04) equals the deployed pin, actions/attest@1e69f48acb82 # v4.2.2 at publish-catalog.yml:138, 145 and 252. The layer input's 'unpinned' is a catalog-field artifact.

INCUMBENCY. Each winner's standing rests on configuration or a stale run on one axis.
- zizmor: the scoped-permissions axis has no negative control (gap 1), and it has no AI-agent audit (above).
- actions/attest: the hosted 0/1/0 qualification (run 35541322881, 2026-09-20) predates the 2026-09-22 workflow changes (gap 2).
- syft: whole-runtime inventory rests on one local run on one SDK prefix (gap 3).
- macOS arm64 is untested for all three.

ALTERNATIVES HEALTH.

The repository already replaced it with kjanat/actionlint 1.17.0 on 2026-09-28 (validate.yml:88-103). kjanat is maintained (259 commits since 2026-07-11; latest v1.17.0 equals the pin), so the layer's alternatives list should name kjanat.

I'm shifting my focus to Betterleaks'. The last release was v8.30.1 (2026-03-21) and the last default-branch commit 2026-07-22, so it crosses the 90-day line on 2026-10-20 absent a new commit.

proposed.demonstrated_gap: Neither winner yields a revision-pinned protocol verdict. The Inspector's retained receipts are one stdio arithmetic call and a tools/list pass (open gap 4 is 'advanced', not settled). mcporter's CHANGELOG@v0.14.2 L236-L240 claims 2026-07-28 support (server/discover probe, legacy initialize fallback, per-server protocolVersion) and a `mcporter serve` endpoint that 'answers 2026-07-28 and 2025-era clients'. The stack has never measured either claim. The 2026-07-28 revision removed sessions and the initialize handshake, made server/discover mandatory and required ttlMs/cacheScope plus Mcp-Method/Mcp-Name headers (official changelog). Era negotiation is now where a bridge or inspector can silently diverge. The upstream suite ships frozen per-revision requirement sets for 2025-11-25 and 2026-07-28 (the latter anchored at 0.2.0-alpha.10). It supports --requirements and --expected-failures on both a client leg (--command) and a server leg (--url), and npm 0.2.0-alpha.12 publishes both requirement files. It would complement the Inspector as the layer's acceptance harness, not replace it. The 2026-09-29 sweep refuted that proposal on two false premises: that no published artifact carried --requirements, and that a read-only check could not tell. Corrected, those premises favor this label, and the Claude fit refuter wrote 'UNDER-LABELED: relabel as targeted_candidate'. Both premises are corrected here with the npm and jsDelivr evidence.

Client leg: `client --command <thin wrapper over mcporter call>`, and the same for the Inspector CLI and mcpdo, at both revisions. Keep it as the acceptance harness if three reruns give identical per-scenario verdicts and at least one protocol-level scenario (server-stateless, caching, request-metadata, dns-rebinding-protection, input-required-result-*) gives a verdict that Inspector tools/list receipts cannot express. proposed.demonstrated_gap: No bridge, inspect or configure gap for this layer. Its distinctive controls act only on traffic routed through the proxy: new-server quarantine, tool-level SHA-256 re-quarantine, scanner integration, and v0.70.0's profile tool tiers with per-client mcp_cli_ credentials. Routing native Claude Code/Codex traffic through it folds Claude Code's per-server deferral and permission into one proxied server. That was the 2026-09-29 fit refutation, and v0.70.0 adds nothing that changes it. The v0.70.0 notes make no 2026-07-28 claim. They record a v0.69 defect in which restarts could overwrite a held server's quarantine (fixed in #1485/#1488), the very state an examination stage would rely on. Claude Code documents allowedMcpServers/deniedMcpServers under managed MCP configuration as a native way to restrict connections to reviewed servers; the managed-mcp page itself was not opened here. The handoff's own comparison (retrieve_tools/describe_tool against native deferral) is a token-efficiency arm owned by overlap-token.
proposed.comparison_that_would_overturn: Reopen here only if a reviewed server must run under continuous tool-change detection. Use one pinned fixture whose tool description is mutated between sessions. The proposal stands if mcpproxy v0.70.0 or later blocks the changed tool on the proxied path while direct native registration does not. Call results must stay identical, and Claude Code tool deferral must be preserved through the OmniRoute route (same ToolSearch behavior with and without the proxy).

proposed.demonstrated_gap: The current inspection winner's own package now ships a daemon bridge in mcporter's role ('Native CLI bridge with persistent MCP daemon connection'). Inspector 2.10.0 (2026-10-07) adds mcpdo (PR #1783): 'an experimental connection CLI … connect to an MCP server once, then run many commands against that named connection (ssh-agent style)'. Connections are held by an implicit local Unix-socket daemon with a per-daemon bearer token and 0700 socket directories. Terminal output is sanitized of control characters. It shares oauth.json with the other Inspector clients and signs in at connect time (--relogin, --stored-auth-only). It negotiates legacy and modern protocol eras and has 417 tests behind a 90% coverage gate. The same release adds core 'crashable stdio fixture + mid-session crash reconciliation tests' (PR #2598) and adopts ext-tasks (PR #2564). 2.10.1 (2026-10-08) restores the `npx @modelcontextprotocol/inspector` command, which the new mcpdo bin had broken. The stack pins 2.9.0. mcporter's daemon needed a manual archive after SIGKILL and stayed failed after SIGSTOP (9-induced…json L33-50). mcpdo's README documents no automatic reconnect, and its daemon `mcpdod` can be killed with `pkill mcpdod`, so its recovery is an untested boundary. mcpdo is the MCP organization's official bridge, not a third-party gateway.

Also check that a second uid cannot command the daemon without its token. mcpdo replaces mcporter if call outcomes match on the retained set and it recovers with zero manual steps where mcporter required archiving daemon/user.json. proposed.demonstrated_gap: This layer has never judged page-defined tools. Since v0.0.82 (2026-09-18), playwright-mcp offers the tools a page registers through WebMCP as `webmcp_<tool>`, on by default. They carry the page's own input schema and annotations, the list follows the current tab, and clients receive tools/list_changed. Upstream's own note says: 'Tool names, descriptions, schemas and results come from the page, so treat them as untrusted input'. Opt-outs are `--no-webmcp`, `PLAYWRIGHT_MCP_WEBMCP=false` or config `webmcp: false` (README L438; 'Enabled by default' at L670). v0.0.83 bundles the same Playwright 1.64.0-alpha-1790635538000 as the stack's playwright-cli pin. By construction, these are unexamined tool entries entering the agent's MCP tool list. The WebMCP spec §6.3.1.1 names 'Metadata / Description Attacks (Tool Poisoning)' by malicious websites, and §6.3.2 warns that a tool's declared intent may not match its behavior. Stack winners already reach the same tools without MCP-native injection. playwright-cli 0.1.22 has `webmcp-list`/`webmcp-call` (since v0.1.20), and agent-browser has `webmcp list`/`webmcp invoke` (per SKILL.md at v0.38.2; the CLI command surface was not separately verified). playwright-mcp's only added capability is MCP-native exposure, with no measured advantage. The ledger shows it only in web-research's landscape-sweep-20260923-attempt-1 with votes not_returned (catalogs/saturation/ledger.json:246), so it was never judged.
proposed.comparison_that_would_overturn: Use a frozen local WebMCP fixture page (Chromium 155+ with --enable-features=WebMCP) that registers 3 tools: one benign, one with a poisoned description (spec §6.3.1.1), and one whose declared intent is misrepresented (§6.3.2). Arms: (a) playwright-mcp v0.0.83 default; (b) playwright-mcp --no-webmcp; (c) playwright-cli 0.1.22 webmcp-list/webmcp-call, with config webmcp on and off; (d) agent-browser 0.38.2 webmcp list/invoke. Per arm, record task success, tool calls, tokens, latency, and whether the poisoned tool is called or changes later actions. Gate checks: a Claude Code deny rule `mcp__playwright__webmcp_*` keeps tools added through list_changed out of context; mcporter `allowedTools` hides them; Inspector 2.10.1 lists them after navigation; Codex exact-name `enabled_tools` behaves as documented (issue #47102 is open). Promote to targeted_candidate only if (a) beats both CLI arms on success or tokens while a gate keeps the poisoned tool from being called in 3/3 runs.

proposed.demonstrated_gap: This is the specification, not an installable component. It is a Draft Community Group Report dated 8 October 2026, with no GitHub release; license NOASSERTION under the W3C CLA (information only). It defines the surface that any page-tool gate must reason about. The API is `document.modelContext.registerTool()`, `getTools()` and `executeTool()` (README L268-383), and a page can disable it with `Permissions-Policy: tools=()` (L333). Its §6 security considerations name tool poisoning (§6.3.1.1) and misrepresentation of intent (§6.3.2). Agent-side user confirmation appears only as an open exploration (README L529). Browser support: a Chrome 149 origin trial plus a local flag, an Edge 150 origin trial, and ChatGPT Desktop; Firefox and Safari have standards positions only. The stack has no recorded position on whether page tools reach its agents. It should track this spec as the reference for that decision, not adopt it.
proposed.comparison_that_would_overturn: Reassess, and promote a browser-lane gate to a targeted trial, when either (a) WebMCP ships unflagged in stable Chrome, so ordinary pages expose tools to the stack's browser lanes by default, or (b) the spec or its WPT suite (wpt.fyi/results/webmcp) defines an agent-side consent mechanism. Either would be measured on a fixture page: an unconsented page-tool call is blocked in playwright-cli or agent-browser, while consented calls succeed.

(5) TRUE: Playwright v1.64.0 adds page.webmcp and frame.webmcp; its example uses --enable-features=WebMCP. (6) TRUE: v1.64.0 notes and playwright-mcp README L438/L670. (7) FALSE as stated: webmcp-gen is not installed. adoption/skills/manifest.json:924 is excluded[26], 'Served by the pinned agent-browser CLI through `agent-browser skills get <name>`'. Its SKILL.md (identical at v0.38.2 and main, sha256 prefix aca7fc9e74463aaa) is an authoring and validation workflow: it writes webmcp.init.js, manifest.json and eval.json and requires a malicious-description eval case. It does not cover gating page tools that an MCP server offers to an agent.

CAN INSPECTOR OR MCPORTER LIST OR GATE PAGE-DEFINED TOOLS? Inspector 2.10.x lists whatever tools/list returns. Whether it shows webmcp_<tool> after a navigation (via tools/list_changed) is untested. Its new TUI '/' filter (PR #2578) only filters the view; it is not a gate, and the 2.10.0/2.10.1 notes contain no allow or deny control. mcporter can gate: `allowedTools` is an exact-name allowlist ('Only listed tools appear in mcporter list and can be called', docs/config.md L242), which hides any dynamic webmcp_<tool>. `blockedTools` also takes exact names only (L243), so it cannot catch dynamic names. Native gates: Claude Code deny and ask rules accept tool-name globs (documented; untested for tools added through list_changed). Codex has exact-name enabled_tools/disabled_tools plus default_tools_approval_mode; issue #47102 (enabled_tools yields zero tools) has been open since 2026-09-21. Upstream switches: playwright-mcp --no-webmcp, and playwright-cli config `webmcp: false`.

CROSS-LAYER FLAG FOR WEB-RESEARCH (highest priority): the pinned playwright-cli 0.1.22 winner already puts page-registered WebMCP tool names, descriptions and input schemas at the top of every page snapshot by default (v0.1.21 notes; opt out with config `webmcp: false`). It also has webmcp-list and webmcp-call (v0.1.20). This is the live page-tool surface in the stack today, more than playwright-mcp, which the stack has not adopted. playwright-test is pinned at 1.63.0; upstream v1.64.0 (2026-10-07) adds page.webmcp.tools() and callTool(), a deterministic, lockable inspector for page tools.

WINNER HEALTH. mcp-inspector: not archived or renamed. The installed pin is 2.9.0 and upstream is 2.10.1 (2026-10-08). 2.10.0 added mcpdo, ext-tasks, crash-reconciliation tests and catalog writes; 2.10.1 restored the npx bin. GitHub reports the license as NOASSERTION, while the stack records an Apache-2.0 AND MIT relicensing transition (information only). mcporter: not archived. v0.14.2 (2026-10-01) is the latest release and matches the installed pin; MIT. The sealed verdict text still names pins 0.13.13 and 2.7.0, against installed 0.14.2 and 2.9.0, so that text is stale.

INCUMBENCY. mcporter's standing as the bridge rests on bridge-call receipts and a three-bridge matched set. Its recovery was measured as not automatic: SIGKILL required a manual archive; after SIGSTOP the next call failed in 60.3 s, and recovery stayed false even after the daemon was killed (9-induced…json L33-50, L76-93). No receipt compares it with the clients' own MCP reconnect and OAuth (Claude Code 2.1.295, Codex 0.158-0.162) or with mcpdo, so for those functions it holds its place by incumbency. mcp-inspector's inspection standing rests on a stdio arithmetic call and tools/list receipts only.

The installed codex-cli 0.161.0 describes `codex doctor` only as 'Diagnose local Codex installation, config, auth, and runtime health' (help text; this absence claim is bounded to that output). skills-ref 0.1.0 checks SKILL.md format only, and the native Claude-side /doctor prompt-audit (Claude Code 2.1.283) covers Claude files only; both facts come from the prior fit record and were not re-verified here. Yet Codex loads AGENTS.md and the trial's 28 pinned SKILL.md files (Codex-enabled description chars 10,055 against a 6,000-token configured budget). agnix v0.57.0 (2026-10-08) is a CLI linter with no per-task context cost. Its README table lists AGENTS.md rules (AGM-*/XP-*, 13), Agent Skills rules (AS-*/CC-SK-*, 31), Claude Code rules (CC-*, 53) and MCP rules (12). Its released [0.57.0] changelog says 'Review Claude Code 2.1.294' and 'Accept Codex 0.161 Daybreak settings'. Prior record: the 2026-09-23 sweep kept agnix as keep_but_compare with 'no demonstrated gap'. On 2026-09-26 the Claude fit refuter rejected it (0.65) on four grounds: (a) native prompt-audit precedence; (b) v0.54.0 tracked only Claude Code 2.1.273; (c) a circular false-positive-only trial with no known positives; (d) one human maintainer and no release provenance. GPT-6 did not refute it (0.88). This proposal: answers (b) with the released changelog (the Unreleased Codex 0.162 and Claude 2.1.295 lines are excluded); narrows (a) to the Claude side, because Codex has no native equivalent per its installed help; replaces (c) with a seeded known-positive design; and keeps (d) as recorded facts, not exclusion grounds. Published reference for the defect class: arXiv:2606.15828 (SCAM 2026), the first catalog of smells for coding-agent configuration files, with six smells and automated detection heuristics. agnix's own skills, /agnix command and agent are out of scope; the trial uses the CLI binary only.

Seed it with at least 12 known-positive defects from classes both tools claim: dead file references; missing skill references; over-cap or oversized descriptions; invalid skill names and directory mismatches; contradictory rules across AGENTS.md levels; unknown config keys. Keep an unseeded clean checkout beside it. Adopt agnix as a pre-commit/CI lint if it reports at least one Codex-side seeded defect class that no installed tool reports and holds precision of at least 0.8 on the clean checkout. Refute if prompt-audit plus existing checks match its recall, or if its clean-checkout false-positive rate exceeds 0.2.

proposed.demonstrated_gap: The 09-26 gap still holds on origin/main 2ecce6ec (2026-10-08). The Collector's host_metrics receiver scrapes only cpu, memory, load and filesystem, and the pipeline has no accelerator series. VRAM, utilization, power, temperature and clock history therefore cannot be reconciled with llama-server/vLLM engine counters inside the one privacy-filtered pipeline. The li26 guard reads ad-hoc 1 Hz nvidia-smi samples outside it, and production C2 peaks at 20,314 MiB, leaving 3,829 MiB free, with no free-memory guard. Upstream is maintained: v1.15.1 is still the latest release, and the 30 main commits since 2026-09-03 are dependency and CI updates, so the tag needs no commit pin. Re-read on 2026-10-09, NVIDIA's CUDA-on-WSL guide v13.4 section 5.2 still says 'GPU utilization, active compute process are some queries that are not yet supported'. The unretained 09-26 idle probe nonetheless got device-level answers in WSL, so utilization under load is the untested boundary. Per-process fields cannot be compared through NVML on either side. This proposal deliberately replaces the critic's literal 'Windows-host exporter scraped by WSL Prometheus'. --nvidia-smi-command takes a full Windows path, so a second WSL-side instance can read nvidia-smi.exe through interop as the WDDM reference. That gives the same Windows reading without a Windows listener, and keeps both endpoints on loopback.
proposed.comparison_that_would_overturn: Bounded WSL trial. Run v1.15.1 as a systemd --user unit with --web.listen-address=127.0.0.1:9835 and --no-collect.compute-apps, dropping the uuid, serial and pci labels at scrape. Run a second instance on 127.0.0.1:9836 with --nvidia-smi-command pointed at the Windows nvidia-smi.exe through interop, as the WDDM reference. The adopted Prometheus scrapes both during one li26 replay on production llama-server C2, with the vLLM embedding service resident and window.sh left as the guard. Adopt only if all of these hold: (a) memory.used/free agree with window.sh within 1 MiB on at least 99% of pairs; (b) under that load, WSL utilization.gpu stays within 5 percentage points of the WDDM reference, which tests NVIDIA's section 5.2 caveat directly; (c) induced failures show in the command_exit_code series, not as healthy-looking gaps; (d) background polling adds no window.sh latency or guard timeouts; (e) one cross-signal query works that the ad-hoc files cannot answer, such as vLLM kv_cache_usage_perc against memory.used. A one-off --collect.compute-apps run is recorded as an expected negative on both sides, not as a criterion. (1) FP-CHECK OF THE CRITIC'S CLAIMS: 2 TRUE, 2 PARTIALLY TRUE, 2 FALSE.
(a) 'Ollama v0.40.0 (2026-09-25) runs MLX by default on Apple Silicon': PARTIALLY TRUE. The behavior is verbatim in the release body, and the release is prerelease=false. But 2026-09-25T03:31:52Z is the publish time the promoted release object kept from v0.40.0-rc0, as recorded by the 09-26 sweep. (c) 'prism-ml has no GitHub account': FALSE as worded. https://github.com/prism-ml is an Organization with 0 public repositories; its ownership is unverified. Prism ML's code lives under PrismML-Eng, which the HF card links: llama.cpp, mlx and mlx-swift forks, plus Bonsai-demo.
(d) 'JetBrains/Mellum is stale by the 90-day rule': TRUE. Its last default-branch commit is 2025-07-29T15:07:54Z, nowhere near the 2026-07-11 boundary.
(e) 'The model axis stops at DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash, 2026-09-10': PARTIALLY TRUE. None of the named models has an entry of its own. But the sweep input work/models.json, under Qwen/Qwen3.8-27B limitations[3], already records two of them from li26 (2026-09-26): MiMo-V2.6-Distill-Qwen-9B was measured and failed non-inferiority, and Ternary Bonsai 2 27B was runtime_unsupported. (f) 'Compare a Windows-host exporter's per-process fields with in-WSL NVML': FALSE as an NVML comparison. Active compute process queries are unsupported under WSL (section 5.2), and the 09-26 probe on this workstation found per-process memory N/A on both sides. NVIDIA's nvidia-smi doc saying WDDM per-process memory is unavailable is carried from 09-26 and was not re-fetched this round. Utilization is the field that can be compared. Proposal 2 therefore replaces the Windows listener with a second WSL-side exporter instance that runs nvidia-smi.exe through interop. The only Windows per-process path, windows_exporter's GPU perf counters, was refuted on 09-26, and whether WSL CUDA work appears in those counters is unverified.

(2) MODEL AXIS (HF-only), for the coordinator to record in work/models.json. This worker did not write the shared file. All facts below come from hf models info and hf models card on 2026-10-09.

The card's own path is custom joint_schema_model.py (repo code), tested in BF16 on an H200. Card evals are Decision Index 0.2.1 (internal run) and Typesafe workflow evals; for example FinEntity macro-F1 96.2 and median latency 209.3 ms. There is no 8-K item evaluation. Its card is identical apart from names, with FinEntity 97.1 and median latency 38.8 ms. It shares MiMo-9B's base, but a decision head is a different mechanism, so MiMo's failure does not transfer. Clef and Clef-Flash are the only new models that warrant a NEW frozen plan. Arms: (a) a physical cross-host restore from the WSL2 workstation to the Mac (baseline), (b) a fresh apple/container 1.5.0 Linux guest, (c) a fresh Tart 2.40.1 macOS guest cloned by digest and run with --net-softnet, and (d) a fresh Lume macOS guest. Tart becomes a targeted_candidate only if arm (c) catches a Mac-bootstrap or restore defect that (a) and (b) miss, at equal or lower cost than (d). proposed.demonstrated_gap: None for hosting. The README describes srt as 'a lightweight sandboxing tool for enforcing filesystem and network restrictions on arbitrary processes'. It is aimed at agents, local MCP servers and bash commands, and is labelled a 'Beta Research Preview' (README L3-9). It does not host long-running network services. On Linux 'the network namespace of the sandboxed process is removed entirely', and all traffic goes through host proxies over bind-mounted Unix sockets (L124). Seccomp blocks socket(AF_UNIX) creation by default (L943). allowLocalBinding defaults to false (L427). A FastAPI, Next.js or PostgreSQL listener inside srt would therefore not be reachable from host clients unless those defaults are weakened. That is an inference from the README; it was not executed. Supervision for this layer is already settled on systemd (open_gaps_followup index 4). The 2026-09-29 sweep already refuted srt on fit in the isolation layer, where it belongs. proposed.demonstrated_gap: The packet leaves macOS hosting unqualified. Apple Container provides an upstream-supported way to run the selected Linux services as lightweight VMs on Apple Silicon, using OCI images. Its 1.5.0 release also fixes container egress after localhost DNS changes and a Kubernetes-plugin vulnerability, both absent from the supplied 1.4.1 pin. This warrants a bounded Mac qualification; it does not establish superiority over native hosting or Podman. macOS 26 is a prerequisite.
proposed.comparison_that_would_overturn: On the 24 GB and 64 GB Macs running macOS 26, compare 1.5.0 with native services and Podman Machine, holding application versions and data constant. Run the complete application acceptance, 20 crash/restart cycles, host reboot, and logical database restore onto the other physical Mac. Require zero lost committed records, only declared network exposure and persistent state, and complete frontend recovery. Select it if those gates pass and its isolation benefit comes with no more than 10% throughput loss versus native; compare total host memory and recovery time directly with Podman.

Research used the requested 2026-10-09 cutoff and a 90-day window starting 2026-07-11. Counts are per attempted query or URL, including failed attempts: three search queries and four initial GitHub-URL requests failed because the web route returned an unknown-route error. The fetch fallback successfully retrieved GitHub REST and primary documentation. Local skill reads and searches within already retrieved content are excluded from these counts. No candidate was installed or executed. Comparison thresholds above are proposed qualification rules, not measured results. Nonempty one-result commit queries establish maintenance eligibility, not OpenSSF's weekly-activity top score. Stars and license classifications did not affect ranking.

The fourth seed, https://github.com/openai/orchard, was assessed but omitted from the six proposals: not_adopted for the present local application requirement. Its [versioned README](https://github.com/openai/orchard/blob/0.57.0/README.md) describes orchestration of Tart VMs across Apple Silicon machines, adding a controller/worker system without a demonstrated fleet-scheduling requirement here. [Release 0.57.0](https://github.com/openai/orchard/releases/tag/0.57.0), published September 15, includes useful directory-sharing, capacity-accounting and controller-recovery changes. [Metadata](https://api.github.com/repos/openai/orchard) confirms canonical ownership, archived=false and NOASSERTION; [the default-branch query](https://api.github.com/repos/openai/orchard/commits?since=2026-07-11T00:00:00.000Z&per_page=1) returned a September 24 commit, so it passes the maintenance rule despite lower recent activity. Reconsider when pooled VM scheduling is required and a paired trial against direct Tart demonstrates better completed-job throughput or worker-loss recovery without unacceptable memory overhead. License was not a rejection reason.

Winner health changed since the packet: [FastAPI 0.143.0](https://github.com/fastapi/fastapi/releases/tag/0.143.0), published October 8, supersedes the reported 0.142.4 and makes automatic OpenTelemetry exporter setup opt-in. An upgrade comparison should therefore hold telemetry configuration explicit. [Next.js v16.4.0](https://github.com/vercel/next.js/releases/tag/v16.4.0) remains the current release; the comparison control should use the packet's installed 16.3.8 rather than its sealed-verdict 16.3.5. [PostgreSQL's official version table](https://www.postgresql.org/support/versioning/) identifies 18.6 as the current supported 18.x minor and advertises 19 Beta 4, not a stable 19 replacement. PostgreSQL's GitHub latest-release 404 is not evidence of abandonment.

Current metadata for [FastAPI](https://api.github.com/repos/fastapi/fastapi), [Next.js](https://api.github.com/repos/vercel/next.js) and [PostgreSQL](https://api.github.com/repos/postgres/postgres) retains the expected canonical repositories, archived=false and the packet's MIT/MIT/NOASSERTION classifications. proposed.demonstrated_gap: The layer has no GPU-job hosting option, although next_action names 'GPU job' as one of its three deployment requirements. The winners (FastAPI, Next.js, PostgreSQL) cover only the CPU web fixture, and open_gaps[3] records that no container lane has run against a workload. The 2026-10-02 architecture selected this toolkit as slot C09 with the engine unresolved, but the slot never reached this packet. Its own evidence_gaps say 'The packet contains no comparison where all named arms ran.' The stack's only measured GPU workload is the native vLLM 0.30.0 embedding runtime (decision local-embedding-runtime, manifests/stack.json vllm 0.30.0). A container route for it, which this toolkit's CDI generation enables on WSL2, is unmeasured on data mounts, rollback, restart and VRAM cost. v1.20.1 carries fixes that bear on this host: the WSL2 NVIDIA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=none injection fix (PR #2025), nvidia-cdi-refresh first-boot device nodes and ordering before Docker and containerd (PR #1979, #2019), and the crun user-namespace rootfs permission fix (PR #1971). Host state, read-only on 2026-10-09: RTX 4090, Windows driver 616.64, 24564 MiB; Docker 29.8.2 client and server; Ubuntu 26.04.1; no /etc/cdi or /var/run/cdi; nvidia-ctk not installed. Supply chain, from the supply-chain-risk-auditor collector: OSV reports no advisory affecting 1.20.1. proposed.demonstrated_gap: The GPU-job path lacks workload qualification in this layer. The stack's C09 artifact already selects NVIDIA Container Toolkit, with Podman and nerdctl shortlisted as unresolved engine choices. That selection does not establish reproducible GPU injection, persistence, rollback or workload cost on the WSL2 RTX 4090. Toolkit v1.20.1 adds a relevant WSL2 device-injection correction and driver-dependent CUDA memory limits. A bounded GPU-job trial could complement the application winners without replacing FastAPI, Next.js or PostgreSQL. Default-branch maintenance remains unknown because the required API request returned HTTP 403.
proposed.comparison_that_would_overturn: Compare the existing native vLLM route against Toolkit v1.20.1 with one C09 engine, initially rootless Podman; retain nerdctl for the unresolved engine comparison without re-proposing Podman. Hold the model revision, precision, prompts, concurrency and application versions constant, and pin the container image digest. Verify explicit CDI device selection and a no-device negative control. Mount weights and research inputs read-only, isolate writable cache/results, restrict networking to the required local scope, and record effective user and privileges. Repeat after a WSL restart and exercise rollback to the previous image with persistent results intact. Proposed acceptance: all existing correctness checks pass, input hashes remain unchanged, restart and rollback succeed without manual data repair, throughput loses no more than 5%, and peak VRAM increases by no more than 512 MiB relative to native. Record cold-start time, job duration and host RAM as additional costs. Test the new memory-limit feature only after establishing its R615-or-later driver prerequisite. These are proposed thresholds, not measured results.

CredSweeper is the reference scanner of Samsung's CredData, the dataset P1 uses. It adds a local, retrainable ML classifier for credential candidates and scans files, git commits and diffs. GitHub's 2026-10-07 move of generic-password detection to a fine-tuned model shows the field moving to ML for this class, but GitHub's version is hosted and paid, which leaves CredSweeper as the local ML comparable. OTHER REPOS CHECKED: praetorian-inc/titus v1.2.11 (2026-10-08), commit efdea19b8420 on 2026-10-08. Its README says it ships 487 rules (L9), derived from NoseyParker and Kingfisher (L546), and documents --validate as opt-in. The 546-line README documents no pre-commit or staged mode. The 2026-09-29 refutation stands: its one unique rule, np.tavily.1, can be ported by configuration. santhreal/keyhog (found by search): created 2026-03-20, so it can be assessed; commit e35457e14174 on 2026-10-07; v0.5.86 (2026-08-25); NOASSERTION; 108 stars. It is a GPU-accelerated scanner with only a vendor-run 25-secret comparison, and scan time is not a measured bottleneck here (55-74 s full history per the parity receipt), so it is not proposed. GitHub MCP server secret scanning went GA on 2026-05-05 and works only 'for repositories with GitHub Secret Protection enabled'; whether that covers this public repo was not verified. GitHub's 2026-10-07 purpose-built secret model is hosted and paid (GHSP/GHAS coverage, AI Credits), so it is excluded under the no-paid-SaaS rule. github/github-mcp-server is itself maintained (commit eb47a99ddb86 on 2026-10-08, v2.0.2). The 2026-09-29 record says push protection is already enabled on this repo; that was not re-verified here.

STACK-SPECIFIC RULE GAP (same for every scanner): no Alpaca (APCA) or Tavily rule exists in gitleaks v8.30.1 (2026-09-29 facts check), betterleaks main (466 ids), trufflehog main (888 detectors) or kingfisher (derived from betterleaks). Titus has np.tavily.1 (2026-09-29). Only a custom [[rules]] entry in the stack's own scanner config (.gitleaks.toml, which betterleaks also reads) closes it, and that beats switching tools. Detecting a leaked paper-broker key before publication falls under this layer, while broker credential handling stays a trading gate.

Open gap 0 (no executed evidence that sign-ins stay off the checkout) is an evidence gap that a working-tree scan (dir mode) can address. No candidate repository closes it by itself.

proposed.demonstrated_gap: The strongest immediate challenger for publication coverage. Stable v1.9.0 adds 46 detection rules; the newer v2.0.0-rc.2 prerelease adds container-layer and image-metadata scanning plus Git pre-receive support. These provide concrete tests beyond the supplied Gitleaks qualification. However, rc.2 also changes Git scanning to --first-parent, creating a history-completeness question that must be tested. These are documented capabilities and a regression hypothesis, not measured superiority.
proposed.comparison_that_would_overturn: Compare Gitleaks 8.30.1, Betterleaks v1.9.0 and v2.0.0-rc.2 as separate pinned arms on Linux/WSL2 x86_64 and both Macs. Use inert fixtures in staged changes, deleted files, merged branches and saved OCI layers; disable validation/analysis and deny outbound traffic. Promote only with additional correctly detected exposures or lower false-positive counts, zero regressions on retained positives, and acceptable publication-gate latency. Any missed merged-branch canary blocks replacement by rc.2.

proposed.demonstrated_gap: Codex's sign-in is a plaintext file wherever the stack runs it, although upstream supports an OS store. Executed on the WSL2 host on 2026-10-09 (HEAD 491aceef): `python3 scripts/credential_status.py --json` reports ${CODEX_HOME:-$HOME/.codex}/auth.json present, mode 0600, outside the worktree. config.toml has no cli_auth_credentials_store line, so the default applies; PR #49361's startup_preflight.rs comment says 'With file auth as the default'. Upstream offers file, keyring, auto and ephemeral. On macOS, keyring maps to the login Keychain (keyring-store Cargo.toml: apple-native), and a keyring save deletes the auth.json fallback (storage.rs). Claude Code and gh already default to the Keychain on macOS, so Codex is the one native sign-in there with an unused OS-store option. Two constraints were verified. (1) The WSL2 host has no Secret Service: org.freedesktop.secrets is neither owned nor activatable on the user bus. Codex's Linux backend is keyring 3.6 linux-native-async-persistent (keyutils plus Secret Service), so there 'keyring' fails and 'auto' falls back to auth.json. (2) The keyring entry is keyed per CODEX_HOME (compute_store_key(&self.codex_home)). tools/sota-convergence/codex_lane.py symlinks the native auth.json into isolated child CODEX_HOMEs (L522-523, L633), so it cannot work under keyring mode. The trial is therefore macOS-interactive only. rust-v0.160.0 (#49118) and rust-v0.161.0 (#49361, #49384) change docs, UI wording and storage-outcome telemetry, not the backend. Installed version: codex-cli 0.161.0.
proposed.comparison_that_would_overturn: On one macOS host, compare a file arm and a keyring arm on the same account. The operator runs `codex logout`, sets cli_auth_credentials_store = "keyring", then runs `codex login --device-auth` in their own terminal. Keyring passes when four things hold. (1) credential_status.py reports codex-native auth.json absent, plus a keychain record once an OS-store kind exists. (2) A `codex exec` smoke succeeds. (3) A token refresh after expiry works without a browser login. (4) No 'falling back to file storage' warning appears across sleep/wake and a locked-keychain SSH session. Keep file storage if any refresh or locked-keychain case fails, or if any tool on that host needs auth.json. WSL2 stays on file until a Secret Service passes the oo7 or gnome-keyring comparison and codex_lane.py no longer requires auth.json.
evidence: https://developers.openai.com/codex/auth: cli_auth_credentials_store values file|keyring|auto|ephemeral. 'keyring' fails if the OS store is unavailable; 'auto' falls back to auth.json; file-based auth.json holds access tokens.

https://github.com/openai/codex/releases/tag/rust-v0.161.0 (2026-10-07): #49361 'Authentication guidance now accounts for keyring storage instead of implying credentials always reside in auth.json'; #49384 tracks credential storage outcomes and redacts sensitive errors.
https://github.com/openai/codex/releases/tag/rust-v0.160.0 (2026-10-01): #49118 'Clarified how provider credentials use the configured storage backend'.

https://github.com/openai/codex/pull/49361: startup_preflight.rs adds 'With file auth as the default, auth.json is a hint of existing credentials. An existing config.toml may select keyring storage, which need not create auth.json'.

https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/main/codex-rs/keyring-store/Cargo.toml (read 2026-10-09): L16 linux-native-async-persistent, L20 apple-native, L23 windows-native; workspace pins keyring 3.6 with default-features=false.

proposed.demonstrated_gap: Measured on the WSL2 host on 2026-10-09: git's GitHub helper is gh. Both credential.https://github.com.helper and credential.https://gist.github.com.helper are '!…/mise/shims/gh auth git-credential'. `gh auth status`, filtered to the token source only, reports $HOME/.config/gh/hosts.yml. That is gh's plaintext fallback (cli/cli internal/config/config.go L418-434), used because this host has no Secret Service. GCM run as the Windows binary from WSL (docs/wsl.md L35-51, L111-118) keeps git's credential in the Windows host store; Windows Credential Manager is the default Windows store (credstores.md L31-35). Git for Windows' GCM is present at /mnt/c/Program Files/Git/mingw64/bin/git-credential-manager.exe (stat only; version unknown, not executed). The gap it closes is narrow. gh still needs its own token for gh api and PR work, so on WSL2 GCM leaves the plaintext hosts.yml token in place and adds a second stored GitHub credential. On macOS, gh (keyring first) and GCM (Keychain default) both use the login Keychain, so there is no gap. GCM has no default store on native Linux, and its Secret Service store requires a GUI session (credstores.md L17, L108). Credentials in the Windows store remain retrievable by any WSL process through interop (`git credential fill`), which the repository guard covers only by command text (secret_path_guard.py L1972-1982). GCM 3.0 breaking changes: macOS 14 or later; a Linux distribution supported by .NET 10. Three published advisories; the newest is GHSA-86c2-4x57-wc8g (2025-01-14, high: a carriage return in a remote URL leaks credentials).
proposed.comparison_that_would_overturn: On the WSL2 host, count the stored GitHub credentials and their kind across the full workflow (git fetch/push plus gh api) in two arms. Arm A is `gh auth setup-git`; measured: one plaintext file, hosts.yml 0600. Arm B is GCM 3.0.1 or later, via the Git for Windows path from docs/wsl.md for git, with gh still used for the API. Arm B wins only if the number of plaintext GitHub tokens on the Linux filesystem drops to 0 while git push and gh api keep working. That could happen, for example, once gh's own token moves to a Secret Service, or once pushes use a separate least-privilege identity. Measure with credential_status.py extended with an OS-store kind, plus gh auth status's token source.

proposed.demonstrated_gap: The WSL2 host has no Secret Service, measured 2026-10-09. The systemd user bus is up (DBUS_SESSION_BUS_ADDRESS set), but org.freedesktop.secrets is neither owned nor activatable. secret-tool, gnome-keyring-daemon, oo7-daemon, kwallet and keepassxc are all absent. That is why gh fell back to plaintext hosts.yml, and why Codex keyring or auto cannot reach an OS store there. A Secret Service provider is the prerequisite for any OS-store kind for gh and Codex on WSL2. oo7 is a maintained Rust org.freedesktop.secrets server with PAM integration, a secret-tool replacement and a git-credential-libsecret replacement. The bridge-style alternatives found (crosskey, keyring_wincred, keyring-pybridge) are language-level libraries that neither gh's go-keyring nor Codex's keyring crate uses. Claude Code (Linux uses ~/.claude/.credentials.json only; its whole CHANGELOG has no keyring or libsecret line) and huggingface_hub (token file; no keyring support found in docs) would not move, so at most 2 of the 4 native sign-ins benefit. The README documents no headless or WSL unlock path; that, and WSL-distro packaging, are unverified. An empty-password or disk-stored unlock secret would be no better than today's 0600 files.
proposed.comparison_that_would_overturn: On the WSL2 host, run oo7-daemon, with the distro's gnome-keyring as the comparison arm, owning org.freedesktop.secrets on the user bus. The operator unlocks it once per WSL boot with a secret that is not stored on disk. Pass requires five things. (1) gh auth login (keyring) and Codex keyring both persist across a full `wsl --shutdown` restart. (2) gh auth status reports token source 'keyring' and hosts.yml holds no token. (3) auth.json is absent. (4) Lanes keep working. (5) The collection is encrypted at rest. Not adopted if unlock needs a password on disk or a GUI, or if Codex auto silently falls back to file after a restart.
evidence: https://github.com/linux-credentials/oo7 (README, main, read 2026-10-09): 'Secret Service provider'. Components: server (org.freedesktop.secrets implementation), pam (PAM integration), cli (secret-tool replacement), git-credential (replacement for git-credential-libsecret), portal. oo7-daemon test command; gnome-keyring-daemon must be killed first.
https://docs.rs/keyring/3.6.3/keyring/: the linux-native-async-persistent feature used by Codex needs Secret Service backing.
https://github.com/cli/cli/blob/trunk/internal/config/config.go: gh stores the token in plaintext when keyring.Set fails (L418-434).
https://code.claude.com/docs/en/authentication: 'On Linux, credentials are stored in ~/.claude/.credentials.json with file mode 0600' (no Secret Service option).

This follow-up prioritizes native credential persistence. The three targeted candidates are bounded qualification work, not evidence that another credential manager must be installed. File storage outside the checkout can satisfy the requirement; OS storage alone does not prove containment across configuration overrides and fallbacks.

No shell commands, installations, candidate execution, credential reads or inventory edits occurred. All comparisons are proposed, not measured. Use the repository's [credential checker](https://github.com/seathatflowsinourveins/native-agent-stack/blob/main/scripts/credential_status.py) and [storage runbook](https://github.com/seathatflowsinourveins/native-agent-stack/blob/main/docs/secret-storage.md) for later metadata-only observations; these supplied repository paths were not fetched here. The supplied layer input marks containment and publication-coverage receipts advanced. This round neither resets those statuses nor certifies their closure.

Publication qualification remains a separate proposed check: use the retained Gitleaks winner in directory mode over the working tree, untracked material and evidence export, with inert canaries. Require detection of every planted canary and publication failure while present, followed by a clean-fixture pass. Repeat on the target host profiles and retain redacted receipts. No such run occurred here.

Winner health could not be refreshed: [Gitleaks metadata](https://api.github.com/repos/gitleaks/gitleaks) and its [default-branch activity query](https://api.github.com/repos/gitleaks/gitleaks/commits?since=2026-07-11T00%3A00%3A00Z&per_page=1) returned HTTP 403. No archive, rename, relicensing or major-release change was verified. The supplied limited integration evidence supports retaining Gitleaks as a control; it does not establish comparative superiority or native-store containment. Retention beyond that evidence rests on continuity, not a demonstrated best result.

The seeded [WIF gateway sample](https://github.com/anthropics/claude-tag-wif-gateway-sample) was omitted because the follow-up explicitly prohibits re-proposing first-round entries. No new federation requirement was supplied, and its previous disposition was not re-evaluated. Other first-round repositories were also not repeated.

Release leads for GCM v3.0.1, Codex rust-v0.160.0/rust-v0.161.0 and Claude Code 2.1.286 remain unverified in this lane; latest-release fields are therefore null. followup_reason.reason: Mechanism: discovery treated the layer as a scanner market. The 8 proposals were 6 secret scanners (betterleaks, kingfisher, trufflehog, CredSweeper, titus, noseyparker), OpenBao and the WIF gateway sample. The requirement's first half, 'keep sign-ins and credentials off the checkout', has no executed evidence (open gap 1), and no proposal looked at where native sign-ins actually rest. That class changed in the last 4 weeks. Git Credential Manager 3.0 shipped as a pre-release on 2026-09-24 and as v3.0.1 on 2026-10-06; it documents sharing the Windows host store with WSL. Codex rust-v0.160.0 (#49118) clarified how provider credentials use the configured storage backend. Codex rust-v0.161.0 (#49361) says authentication guidance 'now accounts for keyring storage instead of implying credentials always reside in auth.json'. Claude Code 2.1.286 fixed macOS sessions that still showed 'Not logged in' after /login while a leftover ~/.claude/.credentials.json existed. adoption/credential-inventory.json (21 entries) records the claude, codex, gh and huggingface native stores only as file paths, with no OS-store kind.
search_directions: https://github.com/git-ecosystem/git-credential-manager (v3.0.1 2026-10-06; last main commit 2026-10-07; GitHub license NOASSERTION, information only). docs/wsl.md shares the Windows host store with WSL2, and docs/credstores.md lists Windows Credential Manager, DPAPI, macOS Keychain, Secret Service and pass. Compare it with gh's own credential helper on where the GitHub token rests on each host: store kind and path, never the value. Record this only through the inventory's own checker, scripts/credential_status.py (runbook docs/secret-storage.md), because the repository's secret_path_guard hook blocks ad-hoc reads of credential paths.

Codex keyring backend (https://github.com/openai/codex/releases/tag/rust-v0.161.0 #49361; rust-v0.160.0 #49118). On WSL2 and macOS, record which store `codex login` uses under each cli_auth_credentials_store setting, and whether ${CODEX_HOME}/auth.json still appears. Record it through scripts/credential_status.py, never by reading the files. That is executed evidence for open gap 1.

Claude Code credential location (https://github.com/anthropics/claude-code/blob/main/CHANGELOG.md 2.1.286, plus the code.claude.com docs). Confirm the macOS Keychain versus ~/.claude/.credentials.json on Linux and WSL2, then add OS-store kinds to adoption/credential-inventory.json so the off-checkout claim can be checked.

Executed off-checkout check: run the gitleaks winner in directory mode over the working tree, untracked files and the evidence/ export path, with a planted canary. The retained gitleaks evidence (checked 2026-09-20) covers one WSL2 host with synthetic inert fixtures.
